{{Short description|Mathematical lemma}}
In [[axiomatic set theory]], the '''Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma''' named after [[Helena Rasiowa]] and [[Roman Sikorski]] is one of the most fundamental facts used in the technique of [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]]. In the area of forcing, a subset ''E'' of a [[poset]] (''P'',&nbsp;≤) is called '''dense''' in ''P'' if for any ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''P'' there is ''e''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''E'' with ''e''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''p''. If ''D'' is a set of dense subsets of ''P'', then a [[Filter (mathematics)|filter]] ''F'' in ''P'' is called ''D''-[[generic filter|generic]] if

:''F'' ∩ ''E'' ≠ ∅ for all ''E'' ∈ ''D''.

Now we can state the '''Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma''':

:Let (''P'',&nbsp;≤) be a poset and ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''P''. If ''D'' is a [[countable]] set of [[Dense order|dense]] subsets of ''P'' then there exists a ''D''-generic [[filter (mathematics)|filter]] ''F'' in ''P'' such that ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''F''.

== Proof of the Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma ==
Let ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''P'' be given. Since ''D'' is countable, ''D''&nbsp;= {&nbsp;''D''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;| ''i''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;'''N'''&nbsp;}, i.e., one can enumerate the dense subsets of ''P'' as ''D''<sub>1</sub>, ''D''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;... and, by density, there exists ''p''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''p'' with ''p''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''D''<sub>1</sub>. Iterating that, one gets ...&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''p''<sub>2</sub>&nbsp;≤ ''p''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''p'' with ''p''<sub>''i''</sub> ∈ ''D''<sub>''i''</sub>. Then ''G'' = {&nbsp;''q''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''P''&nbsp;| ∃''i''. ''q''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;''p''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;} is a ''D''-generic filter.

The Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma can be viewed as an equivalent to a weaker form of [[Martin's axiom]]. More specifically, it is equivalent to MA(ℵ<sub>0</sub>) and to the [[axiom of countable choice]].<ref>{{Cite book
 | first1 = Paul
 | last1 = Howard
 | first2 = Jean E.
 | last2 = Rubin
 | author2-link = Jean E. Rubin
 | title = Consequences of the axiom of choice
 | location = Providence, Rhode Island
 | pages = 17–18
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | isbn = 978-0-8218-0977-8
 | year = 1998
 }}</ref>

== Examples ==
* For (''P'',&nbsp;≤)&nbsp;= (Func(''X'',&nbsp;''Y''),&nbsp;⊇), the poset of [[partial function]]s from&nbsp;''X'' to&nbsp;''Y'', reverse-ordered by inclusion, define ''D''<sub>''x''</sub>&nbsp;= {&nbsp;''s''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''P''&nbsp;| ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;dom(''s'')&nbsp;}. Let ''D''&nbsp;= {&nbsp;''D''<sub>''x''</sub>&nbsp;| ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;}. If ''X'' is countable, the Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma yields a ''D''-generic filter ''F'' and thus a function ''F'':&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''Y''.
* If we adhere to the notation used in dealing with ''D''-[[generic filter]]s, {&nbsp;''H''&nbsp;∪&nbsp;''G''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;| ''P''<sub>''ij''</sub>''P''<sub>''t''</sub>&nbsp;} forms an ''H''-[[generic filter]].
* If ''D'' is uncountable, but of [[cardinality]] strictly smaller than 2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup> and the poset has the [[countable chain condition]], we can instead use [[Martin's axiom]]. However, Martin's axiom is not provable in [[ZFC]].
